issue: Does the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act apply to a debt owed to the United States that arises from a criminal restitution order, where the United States is neither the formal owner nor the direct beneficiary of the debt?

sides.position: The FDCPA does not reach restitution owed to a private party, because the United States is not the holder of the debt in any legally cognizable sense and is neither its formal owner nor its direct beneficiary (Bongiorno; Sobranes).
cases: United States v. Sobranes, 509 F.3d 223 (5th Cir. 2007)
United States v. Bedi, 15 F.4th 222 (2d Cir. 2021)

sides.position: The FDCPA can apply to a debt the Government collects on behalf of a private beneficiary, as held in E.D.P. (the opinion says E.D.P. is a majority opinion that the Second Circuit has cited only once, and that the First and Fifth Circuits have expressly rejected it).
cases: E.D.P. (cited in Bedi; circuit not identified in the excerpts)

quote: In Bongiorno, the First Circuit held that the Government could not use the FDCPA to collect unpaid child support ordered as restitution in a criminal case.
cite: United States v. Bedi, 15 F.4th 222 (2d Cir. 2021)
